rationale: This secondary case-study synthesis of urban water governance in Ghana centrally examines public-private partnership and ownership/regulatory models (corporatization of GWSC into GWCL, affermage vs. the AVRL management contract, independent regulation by PURC under Act 538, and alternative public-people partnerships), making regulatory_model_ownership the clear primary mechanism (with secondary discussion of structural-adjustment user fees/subsidy removal, urban-rural institutional decoupling, and community self-help participation). On the outcome side, the paper explicitly contrasts wide network coverage and income-stratified household piped hookups (primary_connection) with 'deep access' dimensions of water potability/contamination, intermittency/reliability, and per-capita quantity (effective_access) as well as household affordability and informal tanker price burdens (economic_access), warranting effective_access as primary_outcome_family and multiple for assigned_outcome_label_with_multiple. No primary empirical data are collected; the analysis synthesizes published surveys, reports, and secondary literature (systematic_review_secondary).
